name: Heart Failure Clinical Records
healthcare_task: Binary classification - predict death during follow-up in heart failure patients
natural_missingness: None (fully complete dataset per UCI documentation)
computational_needs: Trivial - runs full experiment matrix on an ordinary workstation in minutes
literature_availability: Extensively used as a feature-selection and ML benchmark (e.g. Chicco and Jurman 2020 BMC Medical Informatics)
advantages: Fully complete data gives an unambiguous ground truth for every masked cell, no natural-missingness confound for the complete-data RF baseline, small enough for many repeated GA/seed runs, single well-defined binary target, strong existing literature for RQ4 comparison
limitations: Only 12 features caps how dramatic GA-driven feature reduction can look; modest sample size limits statistical power per subgroup
mcar_mar_mnar_suitability: Excellent - because it starts fully observed, every masked cell has known ground truth, letting MCAR/MAR/MNAR be implemented cleanly at 10/20/30% with no interference from pre-existing missing cells
ga_suitability: Good - 12 features is enough for a meaningful binary chromosome and visible feature-count reduction

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
healthcare_task: Binary classification - CKD vs not-CKD from blood/urine test panel
natural_missingness: Yes - real natural missingness across most columns (age, blood pressure, specific gravity, albumin, sugar, red/white blood cell counts, glucose, etc.)
literature_availability: but categorical encoding and missing-marker cleanup add preprocessing work
advantages: Frequently used as an imputation-method benchmark specifically because of its real missingness
limitations: Richest feature set (24, mixed numeric/categorical) of any candidate, genuine natural missingness is directly relevant to RQ1, well suited to external validation as a possible second dataset
mcar_mar_mnar_suitability: Real missingness means the complete-data reference baseline (Phase 7) must use a smaller complete-case subset rather than the full 400 rows
ga_suitability: and natural vs synthetic missing cells must be kept strictly separate per section 19
score_60: Good, with extra care needed - only originally-observed cells are eligible for controlled masking, and natural missingness must never be counted as reconstruction error
selected: Very good - 24 features and a numeric/categorical mix make GA feature reduction clearly demonstrable

name: Heart Disease (Cleveland)
class_balance: Yes, but minimal (only a handful of missing cells in the Cleveland subset, in the ca and thal columns)
license: Roughly balanced presence vs absence (exact split confirmed at EDA)
advantages: The single most cited benchmark in cardiac ML research, huge body of comparable published results
limitations: Extremely well-established and interpretable feature set; ideal for literature comparison (RQ4)
mcar_mar_mnar_suitability: Small sample size and only 13 features limit how much the study can show beyond replicating well-trodden results; near-complete data means little natural missingness to analyze
ga_suitability: Good for controlled synthetic missingness given how few cells are naturally missing
score_60: Moderate - 13 features is workable but less room to show dramatic reduction than CKD or Cervical Cancer

name: ILPD (Indian Liver Patient Dataset)
healthcare_task: Binary classification - presence/absence of liver disease
literature_availability: Moderate - used in several ML benchmarking studies but less specifically for feature selection or imputation research
advantages: Complete data (clean controlled-missingness ground truth) and largest row count among the complete candidates
limitations: Only 10 features limits GA feature-selection headroom; class imbalance (71/29) is more severe than Heart Failure, weaker literature base specific to this project's methods (imputation + GA)
mcar_mar_mnar_suitability: Good - complete data supports clean synthetic MCAR/MAR/MNAR injection
ga_suitability: Weak-to-moderate - fewest features of all candidates

name: Cervical Cancer (Risk Factors)
healthcare_task: Classification - cervical cancer risk indicators (4 possible binary targets: Hinselmann/Schiller/Cytology/Biopsy)
target: One of Hinselmann, Schiller, Cytology, or Biopsy (all boolean)
natural_missingness: Yes, substantial - many patients left privacy-sensitive questions blank, with some columns very sparsely populated
class_balance: Severely imbalanced across all four targets (positive cases are a small minority; exact rate confirmed at EDA)
literature_availability: Used in some feature-selection and imbalanced-classification studies
advantages: Largest row count and richest feature set (36) of all candidates - the strongest GA feature-selection showcase on paper
limitations: Ambiguous single-target choice among four correlated boolean labels, heavy nonresponse-driven missingness in several columns shrinks the usable complete-case baseline substantially, and severe class imbalance complicates fair comparison across imputation/GA conditions
mcar_mar_mnar_suitability: Weak - the scale and pattern of real (privacy-driven
ga_suitability: likely MNAR-like) missingness makes clean controlled-masking harder to interpret against genuine nonresponse
score_60: Excellent on paper (36 features) but undermined by target ambiguity and missingness overlap
